 Judgment

Present miscellaneous appeal has been filed against the award dated 29.6.2009 passed by Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Fast Track Court), Joura (M.P.) in Claim Case No.
110/2008.

sentences.text: T he facts in brief to decide the present appeal in short are that the appellant - claimants, who was driving the offending vehicle, filed a claim petition under Section 163-A of Motor Vehicles Act before learned claims tribunal for grant of compensation on account of injury sustained by him in a road traffic accident occurred on 09.1.2008 involving mini Truck bearing Registration No. RJ-11/GA 0449.

1
Respondent No. 1 - Owner did not appear before the learned claims tribunal and was proceeded ex-parte.

Respondent No. 2 - insurance company filed its written statement and denied the averments made in the claim petition and further stated that the accident occurred due to negligence of the claimant himself and the offending vehicle was being plied without any valid fitness certificate and permit.
Therefore, the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.

Learned claims tribunal framed issues and after hearing both the parties on merits and recording their evidence partially allowed the claim petition of the appellant - claimant and awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.2,18,600/- which was directed to be paid by respondents jointly and severely and primary responsibility to pay the compensation was fastened upon the insurance company.
Learned counsel for the appellant argued that learned claims tribunal has erred in holding 50% loss in earning capacity of the appellant - claimant.

Since claimant was a driver and sustained 50%
permanent disability in his right leg, loss in his earning capacity should have been held as 100%.
It is further argued that learned claims tribunal has also assessed the income of the claimant on the lower side.
Hence, learned counsel for the appellant prayed that this appeal be allowed and just and proper compensation be granted to the claimant.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the insurance company opposed the prayer of the appellant and argued that learned claims tribunal has rightly passed the award and no interference is warranted in the same.
Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the available record.
In this case, as per the statement of claimant, at the time of accident, he was a driver and was earning Rs.200/- per day, however, he has not produced any document to prove his income.

In the claim petition, at para 1, claimant has pleaded that working as a driver, he used to get Rs.3000/- per month, therefore, the argument of learned counsel for the appellant - claimant is not acceptable that claimant was earning Rs.200/- per day i.e. Rs.6000/- per month.
Therefore, learned claims tribunal has rightly assessed the income of the claimant as Rs.2700/- per month on the basis of facts and situation present before it.

Learned counsel for the appellant further argued that since claimant was a driver, therefore, in view of the fact that he sustained 50% permanent disability, his loss of earning capacity should have been considered as 100%, however, the above argument is not acceptable because Dr. Sanjeev Bandil (AW-2) examined by the claimant in his statement has stated that disability caused to the claimant was 55% only for one leg.
This witness in his cross-examination failed to answer the ratio of permanent disability sustained by the claimant in respect to whole body.

Learned counsel for the appellant cited the case law of Pratap Narayan Singh Deo vs. Srinivas Sabata & Anr.; 1976 AIR 222 and Jakir Hussein vs. Sabir & Ors.; [Civil Appeal No. 2006 of 2015 Vijay Singh vs Sanu Qureshi on 18 July, 2023

entities.text: Pratap Narayan Singh Deo vs. Srinivas Sabata & Anr.; 1976 AIR 222
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46414866/
2 (Arising out of SLP (C) No.981 of 2014); date of judgment 18.2.2015]
, however, the facts and circumstances of the above mentioned cases are different as in this case, claimant has not suffered amputation.
In view of the above discussion, this Court is of the view that learned claims tribunal has rightly assessed 50% loss in earning capacity of the claimant.
However, learned claims tribunal has erred in deducting 1/3rd towards personal expense of the claimant.

In view of the above and as per the Second Schedule of Section 163-A of Motor Vehicles Act,
considering the monthly income of the claimant @ 2700/- per month, 50% loss in earning capacity,
multiplier of 17, Rs.25,000/- towards medical expenses and pain and suffering, total compensation amount comes to Rs.3,00,400/- [(2700x12x17)x50/100 + 25,000/-].
As such, the total amount awarded to the claimant is enhanced from Rs.2,18,600/- to Rs.3,00,400/-.

The enhanced amount comes to Rs.81,800/- (Rupees Eighty One Thousand and Eight Hundred only), with interest at the rate as fixed by the tribunal in the award which is directed to be paid to the claimant by the insurance company in the same apportionment as directed by the claims tribunal.
The enhanced amount of compensation Rs.81,800/- shall be payable to the claimants within 12 weeks from the date of production of a certified copy of this order.
Rest of the award impugned passed by the Tribunal shall remain intact.

If the enhanced amount of compensation is in excess to the valuation of appeal, the difference of the Court fee (if not already paid) shall be deposited by the appellant / claimant within four weeks' from today and proof thereof shall be submitted before the Registry.
Thereafter, Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
Appeal stands allowed to the aforesaid extent and disposed of.

(SUNITA YADAV) JUDGE AKS Vijay Singh vs Sanu Qureshi on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46414866/
